subject: literature
passage: Few residents of the town could remember a time when the Misses Harrow had not quarreled, and fewer still could recall what the original quarrel had concerned. The two sisters, who had shared the narrow house on Crane Street for upward of forty years, communicated chiefly through the housemaid, and each took her meals at a different hour so as never to be found at the same table as the other. ______ so complete was their estrangement that when the elder fell ill one winter, the younger learned of it only from the doctor, whom she happened to meet upon the stairs.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The first two sentences describe how deeply the sisters were estranged. The last sentence pushes that description further with the most striking evidence of all: one did not know the other was ill. A transition that reinforces and intensifies the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something true despite the previous point, but the illness episode confirms the estrangement rather than going against it.
explanation.B: Correct. "Indeed" introduces an even stronger illustration of how complete the sisters' estrangement was.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Consequently" would make the illness episode a result of the separate mealtimes and the messages through the housemaid, but all of these are signs of the same estrangement, and the last sentence presents the most extreme of them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but the last sentence continues the same picture of the sisters.
